keyFacts: Twenty-eighth bishop of Rome, December 17, 283, to April 22, 296
Reigned during the peace before Diocletian’s persecution
Liber Pontificalis calls him a Dalmatian from Salona
Buried in the Catacomb of St. Callixtus, where his epitaph was found
Feast day April 22, shared with St. Soter

faqs.question: Was Pope St. Caius related to Emperor Diocletian?
faqs.answer: A later legend says so, since both were associated with Dalmatia, but there is no reliable historical evidence for the claim.

faqs.question: Was Pope Caius martyred?
faqs.answer: Legend says he was beheaded, but he died years before Diocletian’s persecution began, and early records do not call him a martyr.

directAnswer: St. Marcellinus was the twenty-ninth bishop of Rome, from 296 until his death around 304, and he led the Church when Diocletian’s Great Persecution broke out in 303. Some ancient sources accused him of handing over Scriptures or offering incense under pressure, while others, including St. Augustine, denied the charge. He is venerated as a saint, and his feast has traditionally been kept on April 26.

paras: In February 303, Diocletian issued the first of several edicts ordering churches destroyed, Scriptures surrendered, and Christian meetings banned, followed by orders that clergy be imprisoned and forced to sacrifice. It was the most severe persecution the Church had faced. Marcellinus was bishop of Rome during these years.

The Liberian Catalogue gives the dates of his pontificate, but the Roman calendar of 354 does not include him among the martyrs or the bishops it commemorates, which has led historians to ask whether something about his conduct was disputed.

During the Donatist controversy in North Africa, some Donatists claimed that Marcellinus had handed over sacred books and offered incense to the gods. Augustine rejected this as an unproven slander. Later, the Liber Pontificalis repeated a version in which Marcellinus offered incense, then repented and was martyred, and a document describing a council at Sinuessa where he confessed his fault is now recognized as a forgery.

Historians remain divided about what happened. What is certain is that the Church honors him as a saint. He was buried in the Catacomb of Priscilla on the Via Salaria, and after his death the Roman Church went several years without a bishop.

keyFacts: Twenty-ninth bishop of Rome, June 30, 296, to c. October 25, 304
Led the Church at the start of Diocletian’s Great Persecution (303)
Accused by Donatist sources of lapsing; St. Augustine denied the charge
The story of a council at Sinuessa is a later forgery
Buried in the Catacomb of Priscilla; traditional feast day April 26

faqs.question: Did Pope Marcellinus offer sacrifice to pagan gods?
faqs.answer: Some Donatist writers claimed he handed over Scriptures and offered incense, and the Liber Pontificalis tells of a lapse followed by repentance. St. Augustine called the charge unproven, and the documents supporting the story are considered unreliable or forged. Historians have not reached a firm conclusion.

faqs.question: Why was there a gap after Pope Marcellinus died?
faqs.answer: The persecution under Diocletian and its aftermath made it impossible for the Roman Church to elect a successor for several years. Marcellus I was not chosen until 308.

directAnswer: St. Marcellus I was the thirtieth bishop of Rome, elected in 308 after a long vacancy that followed the Great Persecution. He tried to restore order and imposed penance on Christians who had lapsed, which provoked violent unrest in the Roman community. Emperor Maxentius exiled him, and he died in exile in January 309.

paras: When Marcellus was finally elected in 308, the Roman Church had been without a bishop for several years and its organization had been badly damaged. The Liber Pontificalis says he reorganized the city into twenty-five titles, or parish districts, for baptism, penance, and the burial of martyrs, though historians are unsure how much of this is accurate.

Some scholars once suggested that Marcellus and his predecessor Marcellinus were the same man, because their names and stories became confused in early lists, but most historians treat them as two different bishops.

sections.h2: Penance for the Lapsed and Exile Under Maxentius
paras: Many Christians had lapsed during the persecution and now sought readmission. Marcellus required them to do penance first. An epitaph composed for him later in the century by Pope Damasus says this stern policy angered the lapsed and led to discord, violence, and bloodshed, and that, because of the crime of one who had denied Christ, Marcellus was driven into exile by the tyrant, meaning Emperor Maxentius.

Marcellus died in exile in January 309. A later legend says he was forced to work in a stable set up in a church, which became the origin of the Church of San Marcello al Corso, but that story is not historical. He was buried in the Catacomb of Priscilla, and his feast is January 16.

keyFacts: Thirtieth bishop of Rome, May 27, 308, to January 16, 309
Elected after a vacancy of several years following the persecution
Required penance before readmitting lapsed Christians
Exiled by Emperor Maxentius; died in exile
Buried in the Catacomb of Priscilla; feast day January 16

faqs.question: Why was Pope Marcellus I exiled?
faqs.answer: His insistence that lapsed Christians do penance before readmission caused violent unrest in Rome. According to the epitaph by Pope Damasus, Emperor Maxentius exiled him to restore order.

faqs.question: Is the Church of San Marcello al Corso connected to Pope Marcellus I?
faqs.answer: Yes, it is dedicated to him. A legend says he was forced to tend animals in a stable at that site, but historians regard the story as unhistorical.
